title: span-timeline-playbook-grooming-notes
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a portable playbook-style doc for planning the span timeline (waterfall) surface in the Console trace viewer. Focus: practical interaction patterns for exploring long requests, span grouping, quick filters, and debug-friendly annotations. Intended audience: product, frontend, SRE, and UX who will ship the first iteration (MVP) for Q1 roadmap.

High-level goals (why):
- Help engineers quickly pinpoint latency hotspots in multi-model requests (KV cache misses, routing fallbacks, model switch latencies).
- Make it cheap to triage production incidents without switching to raw logs (link out when needed).
- Provide a compact summary view plus progressively revealed detail (progressive disclosure).

Constraints and assumptions:
- Must work for traces up to 10kms (long traces) and 200 spans without freezing the UI.
- First pass will support server-side timestamps + durations; no distributed tracing correlation yet (future).
- Prefers purely client-side rendering with virtualization for rows.

MVP surface (what to build):
1) Compact timeline (collapsed spans by default):
   - Row per span group (service.action) with count and aggregated duration range (p50/p95).
   - Tap/expand to animate open slot into full span rows beneath.
   - Visual cue for long-tail spans: thin red overlay on portion > threshold.

2) Span detail flyout:
   - Header: span name, service, duration, start offset, tags (key/value), request id.
   - Tabs: Metadata (headers/attrs), Logs (linked), Events (KV/cache hits), Raw JSON (copy).
   - Quick actions: "Copy timing", "Open in logs", "Create ticket" (prefill fields).

3) Filters & quick probes bar (persistent top strip):
   - Text search over span names + attributes (syntax: name:token, tag:key=value).
   - Prebuilt quick filters: long > 500ms, error spans, model-fallback, cache-miss.
   - Toggle: group-by-service / group-by-operation / show-only-errors.

4) Time-slice scrubber and zoom controls:
   - Mini-waterfall overview (Sparkline) with a brush to zoom time ranges.
   - Keyboard shortcuts: shift + drag to select, +/- to zoom, space to play animation.

Interaction notes and micro-flows:
- Expand flow: click on row -> row animates open -> fetch per-span details (lazy) -> arrow to first child span -> keyboard focus goes into expanded region.
- Inspect-range: user highlights a time window in the scrubber -> timeline reflows showing only spans intersecting window; counts of hidden spans shown as collapsed badge.
- Multi-select: shift+click selects multiple spans -> aggregate action bar appears with suggested next steps (trace compare, export, make ticket).

Wireframe description (ASCII sketch for devs):
[Header bar: trace id | duration | region | download]
[Quick probes bar: (search) | [long>500ms] [errors] [cache-miss] [group:service]]
[Mini-sparkline scrubber]\\n--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
| Row 1: auth-service.login (grouped) | #####-----   120ms p95    | [v]        |
| (expanded) child spans:           | [span bars with offsets and red warning]             |
| Row 2: routing (service)          | --###------- 40ms p95     | [v]        |
| Row 3: model-serving (group)      | -----####--- 420ms p95    | [!]        |
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
[Footer: selected span details / copy buttons / open link to logs]

Accessibility and performance notes:
- All interactive elements must be keyboard focusable; aria labels for span durations e.g., 'span x duration 220ms start 1.3s'.
- Use row virtualization and canvas-based mini-waterfall rendering to reduce DOM counts.
- Defer heavy JSON formatting until user opens Raw JSON tab.

Open questions / discussion items (to resolve in grooming):
- How do we represent concurrent spans that overlap heavily? (Option A: stacked lanes per service, Option B: layered single lane with translucency). Decision needed by next sync.
- Should group-by default to service or operation? Metric: fewer clicks for common debug path.
- What threshold values for quick filters are product-configurable vs hard-coded?

Backlog & acceptance criteria (scoped for first 2 sprints):
- RW-2241: Timeline base rendering + virtualization
  - AC: Load traces with up to 200 spans, initial render < 300ms, maintaining 60fps scroll.
- RW-2242: Expand/collapse row groups with lazy span fetch
  - AC: Expanding a group fetches child spans and reveals them; keyboard focus lands on first child.
- RW-2243: Span detail flyout with tabs and logs link
  - AC: Flyout opens within 200ms, logs link is present and opens new tab to logs view with query prefilled.
- RW-2244: Quick probes & filters bar
  - AC: Text search supports name: and tag: syntax; presets shown and toggles update timeline live.

Implementation notes for engineers:
- API: propose trace GET /v1/traces/{id}?level=grouped|full&time_window=start,end. Grouped returns aggregation metadata for each group.
- Client: use react-virtualized for rows, canvas for sparkline. Avoid full JSON parse until flyout open.
- Metrics to capture: render_time_ms, expand_latency_ms, filter_apply_ms, avg_spans_loaded_per_trace.

UX validation plan:
- 3 quick guerrilla usability sessions with internal engineers (15 minutes each) to validate expand/collapse mental model.
- One incident-runbook test: have SRE resolve a seeded slow-model-fallback case using only Console trace viewer; record time to resolution.

Notes to self (brain dump):
- Consider a small 'annotation' feature where engineers can pin a comment to a span (private to org) — high value for knowledge transfer.
- Might want to show model version pins in the span bar for model-serving spans.
- If we support RL fallback, mark those spans with a distinct icon so they stand out in grouped view.

Next steps & owners:
- Design: Elena to produce high-fidelity mocks for stacked-vs-layered overlap options by 2025-11-20.
- Frontend: Raj to spike canvas-based sparkline and virtualization; report perf numbers by 2025-11-28.
- Backend: Samir to draft grouped trace API and example payload by 2025-12-02.
- Product: Maya to host grooming session w/ SRE on 2025-11-12 to decide default grouping and quick-filter thresholds.

Revision log:
- 2025-11-04 Maya created initial playbook.
- 2025-11-12 updated with SRE notes from grooming (meeting minutes linked in Confluence).
- 2026-02-20 added acceptance criteria and ticket IDs for sprint planning.

Unresolved: finalize overlapping span visualization; put on agenda for 2026-02-28 design sync.
